text:
Jordan: quick follow-up from today's all-hands — a few runtime/batching/kernel q's folks asked me to capture here. can leadership or runtime eng chime in?
Ana: thanks Jordan — leaving from the talk. happy to answer where I can; loop in Samir for kernel specifics. :wave:
Mike: first Q — any estimate on p50/p99 improvements from the kernel optimizations we demoed?
Samir: short answer: p50 ~10-12% right now on the experimental path, p99 varies by seq len but ~15-25% lower in our bench harness for 2 models. numbers depend heavily on batching shape.
Emily: are those numbers for 8k context? and q4/q8 quant paths?
Samir: bench was 2k-4k typical; q8 path. q4 still has some edge cases we need to resolve (FP emulation overhead).
Raj: can we get a short doc on which kernels are enabled per model profile? it'd help SRE tune autoscaling.
Lia: +1 on docs. product teams want an explicit mapping so they can set SLOs per route.
Ana: roadmap item: publish a 'kernel compatibility matrix' next week as a lightweight doc. we'll attach examples of perf delta by seq len.
Mike: batching/caching Q — what are recommended batch_size / latency tradeoffs for hosted customers? we had a customer confused by default autoscale/batch settings.
Samir: default continuous batching aims for 20ms latency target; target batch_size varies (we use dynamic thresholding). practical advice: for chat flows set batch_target_tokens=256 and max_wait_ms=8. that usually keeps p99 within SLO and improves throughput.
Jordan: can you paste the config snippet?
Samir: sure:
```
runtime_config:
  batch_target_tokens: 256
  max_wait_ms: 8
  enable_prefix_cache: true
  kv_cache_ttl_ms: 300000
```
Emily: about the kv cache_ttl — we saw evictions causing spikes on some customer workloads. any plan to expose eviction metrics?
Samir: yes — exposing metrics next sprint: kv_cache_hits, kv_cache_evictions, kv_cache_memory_bytes per model. will also add a histogram for eviction latency.
Raj: will the console show suggested cache_ttl based on workload? that'd reduce tickets.
Ana: yep that's part of Redwood Optimize — suggestion engine will propose ttl/batch configs after a 24h sampling window. ETA: end of Q2.
Lia: can we get a quick note on rollouts/compatibility? if a kernel change ships, what is the fallback behavior for Dedicated customers?
Samir: fallback behavior: route policy -> prefer stable kernel, canary kernel flagged per pool. if canary fails p99 or error rate threshold, traffic auto-rolls back to stable. we keep both kernels installed for seamless fallback.
Jordan: is there a plan to make canary results visible in Console? like kernel-specific dashboards?
Samir: yes, viewing canary vs stable perf will be part of the rollout UI — per-route p50/p99, error rate, and token cost delta. aiming for alpha in 3 weeks.
Mike: any breaking changes customers should prepare for (API or config)?
Ana: no API changes planned. some internal metric names will be added — we will document in the changelog. customers on Private deployments may need to run a small upgrade to pick the new kernel package. process will be documented.
Emily: question about quantization support: are we standardizing on q8_0 or q4 variants for default model catalog entries?
Samir: default will remain q8_0 for now for a balance of perf and quality. q4 paths will be 'experimental' models with explicit flags. roadmap to expand q4 coverage in mid-Q3 after more evals.
Raj: who owns the perf regression alerts? we need a pager flow if p99 jumps after a kernel rollout.
Lia: product asks for SLA-friendly notifications to customer success.
Samir: eng-sre will own infra alerts; we will add a 'model perf regression' detector that creates an internal incident and pings #eng-runtime + the rollout owner.
Jordan: action items summary?
Ana: 1) Samir to post kernel compatibility matrix (next week). 2) Samir to add KV cache metrics (next sprint). 3) Console canary dashboards alpha in 3 weeks. 4) Optimize suggestions for ttl/batching by end of Q2.
Jordan: thanks — can we have a 30m follow-up sync? quick opt-in meeting for engineers owning runtimes and product folks.
Lia: yes pls — I can host.
Mike: I'll RSVP.
Emily: adding to calendar.
deploy-bot: scheduled canary: test-pool/kernel-experimental -> started at 2024-04-22T15:18:00Z :rocket:
Jordan: awesome — closing thread but please post links here once docs/dashboards are live. :eyes:
